snippet.title: Taxing Silicon Valley’s Wealth: Joshua Rauh on California’s Billionaire Tax Initiative
snippet.description:
To the certainties of death and taxes, are voters in one of America’s bluest states certain to approve a ballot measure this fall imposing a 5% “wealth tax” on its billionaire class? If so, will California have struck a blow for wealth inequality – or, instead, succeed in killing “the goose that laid the golden egg” as investors and entrepreneurs flee the Golden State for friendlier tax climates? 

Joshua Rauh, Hoover Institution senior fellow in economics and an expert on California-style taxation, discusses America’s current fascination with socialism and economic class warfare as well as all that is at stake in the Golden State. 

Check out this report that examines the revenue and migration impact of the 2026 California Billionaire Tax Act, a one-time 5 percent tax on the worldwide net worth of individuals exceeding $1 billion: https://www.hoover.org/research/net-present-value-billionaire-tax-act-assessment-fiscal-effects-californias-proposed?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=mpp_youtube&utm_content=06302026

snippet.title: What Drives China's Relationships In The Middle East? #ChinaConsidered
snippet.description:
China is often viewed through the lens of its partnership with Iran, but Jonathan Fulton argues that focus obscures a much broader reality. While Beijing maintains ties across the region, its largest investments, commercial relationships, and expatriate communities are concentrated in the Gulf states.

Fulton explains why looking at where China puts its people and money offers a clearer picture of its priorities in the Middle East. Tune in to his conversation with Hoover Senior Fellow Elizabeth Economy on a new episode of China Considered at the "related video" above.

snippet.description:
Veterans are uniquely equipped to solve complex challenges long after their military service ends. Through the Hoover Veteran Fellowship Program, fellows have launched initiatives addressing affordable housing, healthcare access, food insecurity, and support for allied Aghan war refugees, turning personal experiences into lasting community impact.  

The discussion explores how leadership, resilience, and service continue to shape these veterans' work as they build organizations, influence policy, and create innovative solutions. Their stories demonstrate the power of combining mission-driven leadership with collaboration, data, and community partnerships to drive meaningful change.

snippet.title: Indra Nooyi on Leadership and Innovation at PepsiCo | Only In America
snippet.description:
Indra Nooyi is today recognized as one of the most respected business leaders in the world. The former Chairman and CEO of PepsiCo holds 15 honorary degrees, currently serves on the board of Amazon, and is the author of a New York Times bestseller, My Life in Full: Work, Family and Our Future. But this success came as a result of many years of disciplined, hard work by Nooyi across roles, industries, and continents. 

In conversation with Condoleezza Rice, Indra Nooyi reflects on her Only in America story and the values it has instilled in her. Rice speaks with Nooyi about immigrating to the United States; her graduate studies at Yale and early business career; how she rose to leadership at PepsiCo; the importance of innovation to economic growth; what is distinctive about American culture and society; and why she is grateful to be part of the American story.

snippet.title: The Civic Profile: What Kind Of Citizens Are We? | Hoover Institution
snippet.description:
Do you know your civic identity? Do your students and your colleagues know theirs? Our webinar introduces the Civic Profile—a groundbreaking educational and research tool that's redefining how Americans understand their role in democracy. Akin to a “civics Meyers-Briggs,” the Civic Profile is an interactive quiz that holistically measures users’ civic identities across three dimensions: values, knowledge, and engagement. It doesn’t assign grades or pass judgment; rather, the Civic Profile is designed to help Americans understand that democracy requires diverse voices, choices, and actions.

Take the Quiz: https://civicprofile.org/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=rai_webinar&utm_content=06252026

Developed by the Hoover Institution's Center for Revitalizing American Institutions (RAI) and the Working Group on Civics and American Citizenship, the Civic Profile is arriving at a critical moment as our nation approaches its 250th anniversary amid rising partisan division and declining public trust. Webinar attendees hear from early adopters and get an exclusive look at the Civic Profile and how it works, and learn what the research reveals about civic identity in America today.

snippet.title: Choosing Freedom: Courage, Exile, And The Human Pursuit Of Liberty
snippet.description:

The evening also featured human rights activist and Hoover Research Fellow Ayaan Hirsi Ali, Hoover Fellow Abbas Milani, and journalist Joo Sung Ha. Drawing on experiences shaped by Venezuela, Iran, North Korea, and other societies where freedom has been denied, participants explored the meaning of liberty, the costs of tyranny, and the extraordinary courage required to choose freedom.
